summary: r3 is a spec-text-only rewording (zero code delta vs r2, confirmed by the file's own r3-changelog and by nothing in the Files-to-modify / AT list changing scope for the resolve_single_variant fix itself). It corrects r2's single factual mis-statement about which entry point the MCP `grid_search` tool actually rides, and replaces the previously-unsatisfiable single-form AT-2984 with a satisfiable two-leg test. I independently re-verified the three load-bearing source claims underlying the fix rather than trusting the changelog prose: (1) `run_optimize`'s bench closure (`crates/axc-driver/src/optimize.rs:127-134`) is a hardcoded mock returning a fixed `median_ns: 1000` for every variant -- genuinely never dispatches; (2) the MCP `grid_search` tool (`crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/grid_search.rs:321`) calls `bench_variant::handle`, which (`bench_variant.rs:234,279,292,310`) genuinely resolves TEXTUALLY via `compile_source_with_assignments_kernel` and then does real `vk.prepare_kernel`/`vk.dispatch_handle`/`check_correctness` -- it never touches `resolve_single_variant`; (3) `resolve_single_variant`'s only non-test caller in the whole workspace is `crates/axc-optimize/src/grid_search.rs:186`, the library-internal algorithm invoked exclusively by `run_optimize`. All three match §1.2b's rewritten map exactly, so the r2 defect (AT-2984 claiming 'both variants dispatch bit-exact through run_optimize', which cannot happen against a fixed-1000ns mock with `correctness_fn=None`) is genuinely closed, not just reworded away. APPROVE.
strengths: Verified directly against source (not taken on the changelog's word): run_optimize's bench_fn at optimize.rs:127-134 is `Ok(SampleStats { median_ns: 1000, min_ns: 990, max_ns: 1010, n_samples: 1 })` unconditionally -- confirms §1.2b's 'mock bench, measures nothing real' claim precisely, and confirms AT-2984 Leg A's explicit non-assertion of timing/GPU output is the only honest framing available.

Verified the MCP grid_search tool's call graph is disjoint from resolve_single_variant: mcp/tools/grid_search.rs imports and calls only `bench_variant::handle` (line 321), which builds its SPIR-V via `compile_source_with_assignments_kernel` (the textual substitution entry point, bench_variant.rs:234) before dispatching -- this is a structurally different code path from axc-optimize's own grid_search.rs:186 `resolve_single_variant` call. r2's claim that the MCP tool exercises resolve_single_variant was simply wrong; r3's correction is the one supported by the code.

Verified resolve_single_variant has exactly one non-test caller workspace-wide (crates/axc-optimize/src/grid_search.rs:186), which is itself only invoked by run_optimize's mock-benched path -- so the r3 claim 'resolve_single_variant's ONLY consumer is run_optimize' is exactly right, not an approximation.

AT-2984's two legs are each independently checkable against real code behavior: Leg A (no GPU) checks run_optimize's control-flow guarantee (Ok, not NoSuccessfulVariants) plus a static disassembly/metadata check on the written .spv -- both fully deterministic and require no dispatch, consistent with the mock bench. Leg B (GPU) targets the MCP grid_search -> bench_variant path, which is confirmed to genuinely dispatch and correctness-check -- so Leg B is the only leg making a GPU-execution claim, and it's made against the one path that actually executes on GPU.

The r3-changelog is scoped honestly: it labels itself 'spec-text only, ZERO code delta vs r2' and the Files-to-modify table / LOC estimate (~165, cap 300) are unchanged from r2, which I already verified line-by-line in the r2 pass. Nothing in the r3 diff touches the resolve_single_variant ~15-LOC fix, the validate() deletion scope, or the parser/AST/HIR representation -- confirmed by re-reading those sections, which are byte-identical to what I approved at r2.

The downgrade of the r2 headline ('the autotuner truly benchmarks shared-tile variants') to the textual MCP grid_search path, with the non-textual resolve_single_variant path explicitly scoped to 'stops axc optimize failing-closed, nothing more', is the more defensible claim and matches what the code actually does -- this is a strengthening of honesty, not a retreat that hides a gap.
concerns: Minor, carried forward unchanged from r2 (not reopened by r3): QA should still confirm the Coder's resolve_single_variant implementation returns `strategy: None` unconditionally and that the new shared-len substitution loop doesn't get accidentally gated behind existing branches -- this concern is orthogonal to the r3 spec-text delta and was already flagged at r2.

AT-2984 Leg A's disassembly/metadata check on the winner .spv's OpTypeArray length is well-specified in prose but the spec does not pin an exact tool invocation (spirv-dis flag, or which codegen metadata field) -- low risk since either is mechanically equivalent and the spec explicitly allows either, but the Coder should pick one and QA should confirm it actually asserts on the resolved WG value rather than a placeholder.
validation_against_existing: Independently re-derived (not just re-read) the two-entry-point split described in §1.2b by grepping resolve_single_variant's caller set and tracing mcp/tools/grid_search.rs's actual function calls -- the map matches source exactly, confirming the r3 fix addresses a real, previously-mismodeled fact rather than a stylistic nit.

Confirmed the r2 body (parser/AST/HIR representation, emit_module backstop, validate() deletion scope, test delete/keep partition) is untouched between r2 and r3 by re-reading the full milestone file end-to-end at r3 -- consistent with the file's own 'ZERO code delta vs r2' claim.
external_references: https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html (OpTypeArray literal-length semantics unaffected; both r3 AT-2984 legs check length values, not new SPIR-V constructs)
test_suggestions: AT-2984 Leg A should pin the exact disassembly/metadata mechanism (e.g. `spirv-dis` grep for `OpTypeArray %uint <N>` vs. a codegen-metadata struct field) in the AT description or test docstring, so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive which of the two spec-permitted mechanisms was chosen.

AT-2984 Leg B could additionally assert the ranking's ordinal-0/1 assignment values are 32 and 64 respectively (not just 'a ranking is returned'), giving a tighter regression pin on the shared-len variant identity.
summary_final: r3 APPROVED. The single HIGH fix (reworded §1.2b + replaced AT-2984) is verified against source, not just against the changelog's prose: run_optimize's bench is confirmed a hardcoded mock, the MCP grid_search tool is confirmed to ride the textual bench_variant path with genuine dispatch, and resolve_single_variant is confirmed to have exactly one non-test caller (run_optimize's mock path). The correction closes a genuine r2 defect (an unsatisfiable AT-2984) without touching any of the code-bearing design already approved at r2. Zero code delta confirmed. No new inconsistency found.
